In 2009 Muammar Gaddafi used a G8 summit to call for Switzerland to be abolished and split between its neighbours. This is roughly the map he had in mind.

a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ The idea: split the country along language lines. German-speaking Switzerland to Germany, the French-speaking west to France, Italian-speaking Ticino and the south to Italy.
2/ Why? In July 2008 Swiss police arrested his son Hannibal Gaddafi and his wife, accused of beating their servants in a hotel. The couple were held for two days, then released.

3/ Libya struck back: Nestlé and ABB subsidiaries in Libya were shut down, two Swiss businessmen were detained, most flights were cancelled and roughly $5 billion was pulled out of Swiss bank accounts.

4/ The summit was in L'Aquila, Italy, in July 2009, moved there after that April's earthquake. In August, Swiss President Hans-Rudolf Merz flew to Tripoli to apologise, and was heavily criticised at home for it.
5/ The plan has an obvious gap: Switzerland has four national languages, not three. Around 0.5% of the population speak Romansh at home, mostly in Graubünden, and nobody on this map gets them.
6/ The standoff dragged into 2010. One businessman only came home in June 2010 after serving four months. A year later Gaddafi's regime collapsed.
Switzerland survived. But which neighbour would have come out of this plan best? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
